title_original: Visitors’ Lions of the Venice Biennale announced
excerpt_original: The 2026 Visitors’ Lions have been awarded to Nick Cave, for best participant in the exhibition In Minor Keys, and to India, for best national pavilion

blocks.caption: Skarma Sonam Tashi, Echoes of Home (detail), 2026, papier-mâché, clay, MDF board. Photo: Andrea Avezzù

blocks.text: The Biennale di Venezia has announced that the 2026 Visitors’ Lions have been awarded to Nick Cave , for best participant in the exhibition In Minor Keys , and to India , for best national pavilion.

On 9 May, the jury for the 61st Venice Biennale, usually responsible for designating winners of the Golden and Silver Lion awards, resigned . The resignation followed an earlier decision from the jury not to consider the pavilions of any country whose leaders are currently charged with crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court; in effect, Russia and Israel.

In response to the jury’s resignation, the Biennale organisers announced that Visitors’ Lions would instead be awarded at the end of the exhibition. All national pavilions were to be considered for this decision.

In June , an open letter published on e-flux and signed by over 100 artists and teams participating in the 61st Venice Biennale revealed that, as of 3 June, 106 artists had written to the Biennale and publicly announced their withdrawal from the Visitors’ Lions Awards, in solidarity with the jury’s decision to resign. The letter states that the artists’ repeated requests to be withdrawn from consideration were ignored by the Biennale Foundation and its president Pietrangelo Buttafuoco. Neither Nick Cave nor any of the five artists participating in the India Pavilion were signatories of the letter.
